answer: Agent economies can resist Sybil attacks via epoch-renewed memory-hard proof-of-work. Each node periodically submits memory-bound hash solutions to keep its signing key active as sessions wander across endpoints. Because memory bandwidth resists virtualization, attackers incur dedicated DRAM hardware and electricity costs per concurrent identity, even on cheap shale power. However, wealthy adversaries can still fund a tide of fake agents while pricing out lightweight edge devices.
